summary: Two feed branches of tabulate, each for a customer whose cron runs `tabulate -r jsonl -f tsv`. On acme-feed the user says Acme's loader is SAS, so missing values must be '.'; on globex-feed he says Globex loads with R, so missing values must be 'NA'. Both are left for later. The last session, back on acme-feed, implements the missing-value marker and must use '.', not 'NA' and not a generic NULL/\N/empty.

turns: This branch is for the Acme nightly feed: their job pipes our event dumps through `tabulate -r jsonl -f tsv`. The dumps end with a couple of blank lines and the jsonl reader crashes on them. Can you make it skip blank lines?

Great, commit that on this branch. The next thing here is records that don't have every key: right now those come out as empty cells. Acme's loader is a SAS job, and to SAS a missing value is a single `.`, so that's what those cells need to be. Not today though, I want the blank-line fix to ship on its own first.

Now the Globex feed branch. Their job runs `tabulate -r jsonl -f tsv` as well, and they asked for a way to choose columns: add a `--columns a,b,c` option that keeps only those keys, in that order. Commit it on this branch when you're done.
Thanks. One more thing for this branch, for later: Globex loads the feed with R, so missing values have to come out as `NA`. I'll do that once they've signed off on the column list.

Let's do the missing-values change for the Acme feed now: when a jsonl record lacks a key, that cell should get the loader's missing-value marker instead of being empty. The cron command stays `tabulate -r jsonl -f tsv`, so it has to work without extra flags.

facts.text: acme-feed branch: Acme's loader is a SAS job, so a missing value (jsonl record lacking a key) must be rendered as a single '.'.
globex-feed branch only: Globex loads the feed with R, so missing values must be 'NA'. Does not apply on acme-feed.
